AGENTS.md

Source: AGENTS.md

Guidance for AI coding agents contributing to griddy. If you are using griddy on behalf of a user rather than developing it, read the usage guide for LLMs and agents instead.

What this project is

griddy is an R package for exploratory spatial distribution dynamics on long sf panels. It covers classification, classic and spatial Markov chains, chain summaries, homogeneity tests, rank mobility, and ggplot2 plots. The methods come from Rey (2001), Rey, Kang, and Wolf (2016), and the literature they build on. griddy’s contribution is the R implementation: long data keyed by explicit id, time, and value columns, tidy outputs, and class, transition, and spatial-lag labels that stay attached to the results.

griddy is not a port of PySAL giddy. giddy is the validation oracle, not the specification. Results that giddy also computes are checked against static fixtures generated from giddy 2.3.9. griddy’s API follows R and sf conventions, and it deliberately differs from giddy where giddy is wrong (see the Kullback test in ?homogeneity_test). Do not describe griddy as a port, and do not frame changes as “giddy compatibility”.

Commands

devtools::load_all()
devtools::test()                      # all tests
devtools::test(filter = "inference")  # tests/testthat/test-inference.R
devtools::document()                  # after any roxygen change
devtools::check()                     # must report 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes
pkgdown::check_pkgdown()              # every exported topic is in _pkgdown.yml
pkgdown::build_site()                 # see "Website" below

Without an R session tool, use Rscript -e "...".

Architecture

  • R/classify.R: classify_dynamics().
  • R/markov.R: markov_dynamics(), transition_matrix(), steady_state(), class_intervals(), lag_intervals().
  • R/spatial-markov.R: spatial_markov().
  • R/ergodic.R: sojourn_time(), first_passage(), mobility_index().
  • R/inference.R: homogeneity_test(), with the Pearson Q, likelihood-ratio, and Kullback tests.
  • R/rank-mobility.R: rank_mobility().
  • R/plots.R: plot_transition_matrix(), plot_spatial_markov(), plot_rank_mobility().
  • R/data.R: the bundled usjoin panel.
  • tools/oracle/: scripts that generate validation fixtures from PySAL giddy (Python) and from estdaR and spdyn (R).

Conventions that matter

  • Fixtures. Validation fixtures live in tests/testthat/fixtures/, which is Rbuildignored, as is tests/testthat/test-oracles-optional.R. Only that file may read fixtures. A shipped test that reads a fixture passes devtools::test() but fails R CMD check on the built tarball.
  • Regenerating giddy fixtures. Run tools/oracle/pysal_giddy_*.py from the repository root, in a virtual environment with giddy==2.3.9, libpysal, pandas, and scipy. Check the diff: values that should not change must come out byte-identical.
  • New statistics need a reference value from a publication or an oracle in a test, not only a self-consistency check.
  • Documentation. Every exported function has roxygen documentation and an entry in _pkgdown.yml. Run devtools::document() after editing roxygen.
  • Style. Base pipe |> only. Tidy evaluation for id, time, and value arguments.
  • NEWS.md. Add a bullet for every user-facing change under the version being developed.

Website

  • The site deploys from the committed docs/ folder on main. Rebuild it with pkgdown::build_site() and commit docs/.
  • A complete build needs CENSUS_API_KEY (tidycensus), CM_API_KEY (cancensus), and estdaR installed. Without them, the census articles and the estdaR benchmark render without output, and committing that build removes them from the live site.
  • pkgdown renders every .md file in the repository root as a site page, whatever .gitignore and .Rbuildignore say. Keep working notes, drafts, and briefs in the gitignored notes/ folder. Before committing a rebuild, check git status docs for pages that should not be there.
  • pkgdown 2.2.0 and later also writes llms.txt and a Markdown copy of every page.

Writing

  • User-facing prose in vignettes, articles, help pages, and NEWS follows vignettes/articles/giddy-coverage.Rmd: short declarative sentences, concrete specifics, attribution stated once.
  • Cite methods precisely. The degrees-of-freedom adjustment in the homogeneity tests is Bickenbach and Bode (2003).

Boundaries

  • Do not open issues, pull requests, or comments on repositories other than dshkol/griddy, including PySAL giddy. Draft them in notes/ and let the maintainer file them.
  • Do not merge pull requests or push to main without the maintainer’s go-ahead.
